items.title: Stable vertices and the core of a matching do not depend on the reduction process
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 846-849: given a matching, its stable vertices and its core are well defined. The proof (source lines 850-853) is an exchange argument on two reduction processes run on the same matching: one compares the two lists of removed chords, takes the first position at which they differ, and uses the fact that the deviating chord had to become short before being removed in both processes to derive a contradiction, which forces the two lists to remove the same chords. The statement is a well-definedness claim for two constructions and records neither the process comparison nor the minimal-deviation argument, and the argument has to be carried through the vertex renumbering that each removal performs.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled proposition, retained line for line
